hyperedges.label: Backend Resilience Stack (retry, error handler, logging, transactions)

nodes.label: CI Lint and Test Job
nodes.rationale: Runs on push/PR to main and develop with a Node 18.x/20.x matrix: ESLint + type-check, markdown lint, tests with coverage, Next.js build (SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION), and Codecov upload.

nodes.label: Analysis Report: Efficiency, Resilience and Optimization
nodes.rationale: Feb 2026 audit identifying 12 improvement opportunities (3 critical, 5 high, 4 medium) with a prioritization matrix and 3-sprint roadmap estimated at 17-19 hours.
nodes.norm_label: analysis report: efficiency, resilience and optimization

nodes.label: Zod Input Validation Recommendation
nodes.rationale: Zod was in package.json but unused; manual validation in API routes was error-prone and lacked sanitization, so centralizing input validation in Zod schemas was recommended as a P1 critical fix.

nodes.label: Structured Logging Recommendation
nodes.rationale: Raw console.warn/console.error calls in geolocation.ts, crypto.ts and API routes made production debugging and monitoring impossible; a level-based logger routing to monitoring services was proposed.

nodes.label: Centralized Error Middleware Proposal (withErrorHandling)
nodes.rationale: Each API route had its own try/catch producing inconsistent error responses with no centralized logging; a withErrorHandling wrapper mapping ZodError to 400 and everything else to a generic 500 was proposed.

nodes.label: API Cache Headers Recommendation
nodes.rationale: GET API routes queried the DB on every request with no Cache-Control headers; adding private max-age=60 caching was projected to cut response time ~90% and DB queries ~80%.

nodes.label: Rate Limiting Proposal (Upstash Redis)
nodes.rationale: No API route had any rate limit, exposing DDoS/DB-exhaustion risk; the report proposed @upstash/ratelimit with a Redis sliding window (100/hour per IP). The project later chose an in-memory implementation instead.

nodes.label: Items CRUD API
nodes.rationale: Authenticated CRUD over /api/items with Zod validation and ownership checks (401 without session, 403 when not owner).

nodes.label: Shadow Profile Merge Endpoint
nodes.rationale: POST /api/shadow-profile/merge migrates local (anonymous) items into the authenticated user's DB and marks the shadow as merged — the core anonymous-to-authenticated upgrade path.

nodes.label: Anonymized Events API
nodes.rationale: POST /api/events requires no auth by design: events carry only eventType, salaryDaysBucket ranges, 6-char geohash (~610km) and a 15-minute-truncated timestamp so no PII is ever transmitted.

nodes.label: Encrypted Backup API
nodes.rationale: POST /api/backup/create returns an encrypted JSON blob the browser downloads; the user manually uploads it to Google Drive, keeping full control of the encryption key. Restore decrypts, validates structure, and inserts items.

nodes.label: GDPR Consent and Deletion API
nodes.rationale: POST /api/consent (anonymous allowed), DELETE /api/gdpr/delete-shadow (by UUID, no auth) and DELETE /api/gdpr/delete-account (authenticated, requires confirm:true) implement right-to-be-forgotten and consent registration.

nodes.label: Layered Architecture (Presentation / Local Client / API / Services / Persistence)
nodes.rationale: Five layers: Next.js client with SessionProvider, an IndexedDB local-client layer (shadow profile), Next.js API routes, a business-logic services layer (salary calc, shadow profile, encryption), and persistence split between Prisma/SQL and Google Drive for encrypted backups.
nodes.norm_label: layered architecture (presentation / local client / api / services / persistence)

nodes.label: Shadow Profile (Local-First IndexedDB Profile)
nodes.rationale: Local-first design: all data lives in the browser (IndexedDB) so the app works with zero server and offline; a UUID identifies the anonymous profile, and on login items are merged into the user's DB record (ShadowProfile.mergedWithUserId/mergedAt).

nodes.label: Anonymized Event Model (AnonymizedEvent)
nodes.rationale: Privacy-preserving analytics: events store salary-days buckets instead of exact values, 6-character geohashes (~610km squares) instead of coordinates, and timestamps truncated to 15 minutes; userId, description and exact location are deliberately never sent.

nodes.label: Prisma Data Model (User, Item, ShadowProfile, AnonymizedEvent)
nodes.rationale: User (OAuth identity + consent flags) has Items, an optional ShadowProfile, Backups and DeletionRequests; Item carries price, status (pending|purchased|not_purchased), postponedUntil and optional geolocation/geohash.
nodes.norm_label: prisma data model (user, item, shadowprofile, anonymizedevent)

nodes.label: NextAuth JWT Stateless Authentication
nodes.rationale: OAuth via Google, Microsoft Azure AD and Apple with stateless JWT sessions stored in httpOnly cookies (30-day expiry) so no server-side session store is needed.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM Backup Encryption
nodes.rationale: Authenticated encryption via Node's native crypto module: key derived with SHA-256 from ENCRYPTION_KEY, random 12-byte IV, and a GCM auth tag concatenated as iv+tag+ciphertext in base64 — chosen over unauthenticated modes so tampering is detectable.

nodes.label: Contribution Guide
nodes.rationale: Defines branch naming (fix/feature/docs/test/perf), TypeScript standards (no any, explicit types), PR template and process, and bug/feature report templates.

nodes.label: Deployment Guide
nodes.rationale: Covers Vercel (recommended, PostgreSQL storage), Railway, Heroku and Docker deployments; documents critical env vars (NEXTAUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, ENCRYPTION_KEY, OAuth credentials) and a pre-deployment checklist.

nodes.label: Developer Setup Guide
nodes.rationale: SQLite (file:./dev.db) for local development, PostgreSQL for production; documents Prisma scripts (generate/migrate/studio), OAuth provider setup, VS Code tooling and troubleshooting.

nodes.label: Core Web Vitals Targets
nodes.rationale: MVP targets: FCP <1.5s, LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1, FID <100ms, TTI <3s, page size <200KB, TTFB <500ms, measured with Lighthouse/Lighthouse CI.

nodes.label: Caching Strategies (Browser / Server / Redis)
nodes.rationale: Three-tier strategy: Cache-Control headers on API responses, in-memory memoization middleware with 60s TTL, and Redis getOrCache with 300s TTL recommended for production.

nodes.label: Días de Salario Application
nodes.rationale: Web app that reframes prices as days of minimum-wage work to discourage impulsive spending; local-first (IndexedDB), optional OAuth sync, encrypted backups, anonymized analytics, MUI/MS365-inspired accessible UI (WCAG AA+).

nodes.label: Salary Days Calculation
nodes.rationale: Core metric: item price divided by NEXT_PUBLIC_MIN_SALARY_DAILY (241.56) rounded up with Math.ceil, because fractional work days cannot be sold.

nodes.label: Meditation Chamber (Cámara de Meditación)
nodes.rationale: Behavioral design: purchases exceeding 10% of monthly income automatically enter a 72-hour reflection period with a visual countdown; the user can cancel or wait, converting impulse purchases into deliberate decisions.

nodes.label: Financial Health Summary
nodes.rationale: Real-time indicators of 'days of life' committed, under evaluation, and recovered, with nudges when over-committing income and positive reinforcement when cancelling impulsive purchases.

nodes.label: Smart Credit Marketplace
nodes.rationale: Business model: financial-product offers with preferential rates gated by the user's self-control history; requesting information registers the user's 'Meditation Score' as a lead for lenders — better offers unlock as financial responsibility is demonstrated.

nodes.label: retry() Helper with Exponential Backoff
nodes.rationale: Resilience utility used to retry Prisma/HTTP operations with exponential backoff; later centralized into the Prisma client proxy per audit finding R4.

nodes.label: withApiHandler Middleware
nodes.rationale: Centralizes exception capture across API routes, returning a generic 500 and logging with pino — implements the error-middleware pattern proposed in the analysis report.

nodes.label: Pino Structured Logging
nodes.rationale: Server-side structured logging chosen to replace ad-hoc console statements identified in the analysis report.

nodes.label: Privacy by Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Six governing principles: privacy by design (minimize collection), least privilege, defense in depth (6 protection levels from input validation to audit logging), secure by default, user transparency/control, and auditability.

nodes.label: In-Memory Rate Limiting (src/lib/rate-limit.ts)
nodes.rationale: Fixed-window per-IP limiter applied to public endpoints (/api/events, /api/consent, /api/gdpr/delete-shadow, DELETE /api/shadow-profile), returning 429 with Retry-After. Known limitation: state is per-process, so serverless multi-instance deployments enforce per-instance limits; migrate the backend to Redis (e.g. Upstash) keeping the same interface if a global limit is needed.

nodes.label: Per-Handler Session Validation Pattern
nodes.rationale: Deliberate pattern: there is no global middleware.ts — every protected route handler calls getServerSession() explicitly at the start. Rule for new routes: any route touching user data MUST include this check, and userId is ALWAYS derived from the server session, never from the request body.

nodes.label: Consent Anti-Forgery Pattern
nodes.rationale: The consent endpoint never accepts userId from the request body: with an active session it is derived server-side from the session email; without one, consent is recorded as anonymous (userId: null) — because a forgeable consent record is legally worthless under GDPR/LFPDPPP.

nodes.label: Encryption at Rest (crypto.ts AES-256-GCM)
nodes.rationale: Backups are encrypted with AES-256-GCM via Node's native crypto (no external dependencies), SHA-256-derived key, random 12-byte IV and 16-byte auth tag — replacing the previously used unauthenticated AES-CBC so ciphertext tampering is detected.

nodes.label: Security, Resilience and Accessibility Audit
nodes.rationale: Living July 2026 audit with 17 findings (S1-S8, R1-R5, A1-A4); 15 resolved and 2 deferred on 2026-07-08. Key insight: platform-layer features (theme, middleware, headers) were documented as complete but not re-verified as new screens were added, and the lead-selling business model amplifies the legal weight of security findings.

nodes.label: Finding S2: Forgeable Consent userId
nodes.rationale: The public /api/consent endpoint recorded any client-supplied userId into ConsentLog, letting anyone forge consent for another user — critical because consent is the legal basis for sharing behavioral data with lenders. Resolved: userId derived from getServerSession() and removed from the Zod schema entirely.

nodes.label: Finding S4: Zero Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: No API route had rate limits; public unauthenticated endpoints could flood AnonymizedEvent/ConsentLog or brute-force shadow deletion, and could also contaminate the analytics the credit marketplace depends on. Decision: option A (in-memory, no new dependencies) over Upstash Redis — implemented in src/lib/rate-limit.ts with documented per-instance limitation.

nodes.label: Finding R2: Shadow Merge Without Transaction or Idempotency
nodes.rationale: The product's most important flow (anonymous → authenticated migration) used Promise.all of individual prisma.item.create calls: a partial failure left orphaned writes with no rollback, and retries duplicated items. Resolved with prisma.$transaction plus idempotency via mergedAt/mergedWithUserId (retry does not duplicate; merging into another account returns 409).
nodes.norm_label: finding r2: shadow merge without transaction or idempotency

nodes.label: Finding A1: Dark Mode Broken by Hardcoded Hex Colors
nodes.rationale: The theme toggle changed the MUI palette but page.tsx, FinancialHealthSummary and CreditMarketplace hardcoded hex colors, so dark mode (an accessibility feature for photosensitivity/migraine) never activated where it mattered — even though the colors themselves passed WCAG AA contrast. Resolved: zero hardcoded hex outside theme.tsx, all components migrated to theme.palette tokens; rule established: never hardcode hex in content components.
nodes.norm_label: finding a1: dark mode broken by hardcoded hex colors

nodes.label: Finding S5: Missing HTTP Security Headers
nodes.rationale: SECURITY.md claimed CSP/HSTS were implemented but no middleware.ts or next.config.ts headers existed — a doc/reality gap. Resolved via headers() in next.config.ts (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy); CSP keeps 'unsafe-inline' for Next.js/MUI hydration, with nonce hardening as future work.
nodes.norm_label: finding s5: missing http security headers

nodes.label: Testing Pyramid Strategy
nodes.rationale: 80% unit (Jest/ts-jest), 15% integration, 5% E2E (Playwright across chromium/firefox/webkit) with 60% coverage threshold enforced in jest.config.js and an 80% target; Arrange-Act-Assert and test independence as governing principles.

nodes.label: Build Failure: session.user.id Type Error in auth.ts
nodes.rationale: Captured Next.js 16.1.6 build log: compilation succeeds but TypeScript fails — Property 'id' does not exist on session.user's default type when the session callback assigns session.user.id = token.sub, indicating a missing next-auth module augmentation for the custom session shape.
nodes.norm_label: build failure: session.user.id type error in auth.ts
